(Ponchatoula, Louisiana) | college = [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara]] (2025–2026) | draft_year = 2026 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 19 | draft_team = [[Toronto Raptors]] | career_start = 2026 | years1 = {{nbay|2026|start}}–present | team1 = [[Toronto Raptors]] | highlights = * [[West Coast Conference|WCC]] Freshman of the Year (2026) * WCC Sixth Man of the Year (2026) * First-team All-WCC (2026) * WCC All-Freshman Team (2026) * [[Louisiana Mr. Basketball]] (2024) }} '''Allen Graves''' (born July 28, 2006) is an American [[basketball]] player for the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball|Santa Clara Broncos]]. == Early life and high school career == Graves was born on July 28, 2006, in [[Ponchatoula, Louisiana]].{{Cite news |last=Wolstat |first=Ryan |date=2026-06-24 |title=Who is Allen Graves? A closer look at the Raptors' new draft pick |url=https://torontosun.com/sports/basketball/nba/toronto-raptors/allen-graves-closer-look-new-draft-pick |access-date=2026-06-29 |newspaper=[[Toronto Sun]] |issn=0837-3175}} He grew up playing football, but decided to commit to professional basketball as he nursed an elbow injury leading up to his tenth grade. A growth spurt over that summer saw him grow from {{Height|ft=6|in=1}} to {{Height|ft=6|in=7}},{{Cite web |last=Grange |first=Michael |date=2026-06-25 |title=How Allen Graves grew from injured football player to Raptors first-rounder |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/nba/article/how-allen-graves-grew-from-injured-football-player-to-raptors-first-rounder/ |access-date=2026-06-29 |website=[[Sportsnet]] |language=en}} resulting in him shifting from [[point guard]] to a [[Big man (basketball)|big man]] role. In his sophomore year at [[Ponchatoula High School]], Graves averaged 12 points, eight rebounds, and two assists per game as a sophomore. As a junior, Graves averaged a [[double-double]] with 20 points and 15 rebounds and led his team to a Division 1 non-select state championship title. In the championship game, he posted 23 points and 16 rebounds and was named Most Outstanding Player.{{Cite web |date=2023-11-08 |title=Allen Graves Signs With Men's Basketball |url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/news/2023/11/8/allen-graves-signs-with-Bronco-mbb.aspx |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Santa Clara University |language=en}} As a senior, Graves averaged 20.9 points and 12.1 rebounds, leading his team to a 30–4 record. In the state championship game, Graves posted 19 points and 20 rebounds en route to a second consecutive title.{{Cite web |date=2024-03-21 |title=Men's Hoops Signee Allen Graves Named Louisiana Gatorade POTY |url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/news/2024/3/21/mens-basketball-mens-hoops-signee-allen-graves-named-louisiana-gatorade-poty.aspx |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Santa Clara University |language=en}} He was named the 2023–24 Gatorade Louisiana Boys Basketball Player of the Year{{Cite web |title=Allen Graves Gatorade 2023 - 2024: Player of the Year Boys Basketball - Louisiana PLAYER OF THE YEAR |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/Allen-Graves/40227 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260124234125/https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/Allen-Graves/40227 |archive-date=2026-01-24 |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=playeroftheyear.gatorade.com |language=en}} as well as [[Louisiana Mr. Basketball]].{{Cite web |last=LSWA |date=2024-04-07 |title=Ponchatoula's Allen Graves named Louisiana Mr. Basketball |url=https://crescentcitysports.com/ponchatoulas-allen-graves-named-louisiana-mr-basketball/ |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Crescent City Sports |language=en-US}} == College career == After [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] in 2024–25, Graves played all 35 games for Santa Clara in 2025–26. On February 7, 2026, he scored a season-high 30 points and 13 rebounds in a 96–92 win over [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]].{{Cite web |date=2026-02-07 |title=Graves' Career Night Helps Broncos Hold Off Washington State |url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/news/2026/2/7/mens-basketball-graves-career-night-helps-broncos-hold-off-washington-state.aspx |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Santa Clara University |language=en}} As a freshman, Graves averaged 11.8 points and led the team with 6.5 rebounds per game. He also tallied a total of 67 steals, tied for the most among freshmen in D-I with [[Tounde Yessoufou]] and the most by a freshman in program history.{{Cite web |title=Allen Graves - 2025-26 - Men's Basketball |url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/allen--graves/9118 |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Santa Clara University |language=en}} Graves was named the [[West Coast Conference|WCC]]'s Freshman of the Year and Sixth Man of the Year.{{Cite web |date=2026-03-03 |title=West Coast Conference Announces 2025-26 Men's Basketball All-Conference Awards |url=https://wccsports.com/news/2026/2/25/athlete-awards-west-coast-conference-announces-2025-26-mens-basketball-all-conference-awards |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=wccsports.com |language=en}} On April 7, 2026, Graves declared for the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=2026-04-07 |title=Allen Graves Declares For 2026 NBA Draft |url=https://santaclarabroncos.com/news/2026/4/7/mens-basketball-allen-graves-declares-for-2026-nba-draft.aspx |access-date=2026-04-15 |website=Santa Clara University |language=en}} == Professional career == On June 23, 2026, Graves was selected with the 19th overall pick by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[2026 NBA draft]].{{cite news|url=https://torontosun.com/sports/basketball/nba/toronto-raptors/allen-graves-closer-look-new-draft-pick|title=Who is Allen Graves? A closer look at the Raptors' new draft pick|newspaper=Toronto Sun|last=Wolstat|first=Ryan|date=June 24, 2026|access-date=July 15, 2026}} == Career statistics == {{NBA player statistics legend}}{{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team|Santa Clara]] | style="text-align:center;" colspan="11"| [[File:Redshirt.svg|15px|Redshirt]] Redshirt |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2025–26]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball team|Santa Clara]] | 35 || 4 || 22.6 || .512 || .413 || .750 || 6.5 || 1.8 || 1.9 || .9 || 11.8 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Graves' hobby since childhood is reading books, and he has a Instagram page where he posts Bible scripture videos.{{cite news | last = Dickinson | first = Marley | date = July 13, 2026 | title = Toronto Raptors rookie proves he's an old soul with this off-court hobby | url = https://www.blogto.com/sports_play/2026/07/toronto-raptors-rookie-old-soul-hobby/ | work = BlogTO}} == References == {{reflist}} ==External links== *[https://santaclarabroncos.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/allen--graves/9118 Santa Clara Broncos bio] {{Toronto Raptors current roster}} {{2026 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Graves, Allen}} [[Category:2006 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Louisiana]] [[Category:People from Ponchatoula, Louisiana]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Santa Clara Broncos men's basketball players]] [[Category:Toronto Raptors draft picks]]
